title: Readiness Signal stage-2/3 decisions (pipeline/work/<run_id>/decisions.json)
description: Written by the agent following FILTER.md; consumed by publish.mjs (SPEC §5). Documentation only: publish.mjs validates it in code (pipeline/lib/validate.mjs validateDecisions), including the cross-file rules listed in x-rules.

judgments.description: Exactly one per stage-1 survivor in stage1.json; none for anything else.

items.description: Items to publish, in any order: publish.mjs assigns ids (ordered by section, then mechanism), timestamp = slot, backfilled = false.

x-rules: verdict pass + dedup new | material_update | cluster_merged = published: section_tested and draft_index required; items[draft_index].candidate_ids includes the candidate; items[draft_index].section == section_tested.
Each item has exactly one judgment with verdict pass and dedup new or material_update (its primary); cluster_merged judgments add further outlets to the same item.
dedup material_update (pass): match_id = the earlier archive item id and the item's update_of = match_id. An item with update_of needs a material_update primary.
dedup cluster_merged: match_id = the lead's candidate_id (a judgment in this file that is not cluster_merged); verdict, reason_code, section_tested and draft_index equal the lead's.
dedup same_story_dropped: always verdict drop and draft_index null; match_id = the published item id it repeats (same-run duplicates are cluster_merged instead).

Every candidate in an item's candidate_ids exists in candidates.json; a stage-1 survivor attached to an item must be judged pass/published with that draft_index; an extra source registered with add-manual.mjs --extra (extra: true; a public primary source or independent coverage found by search, FILTER.md NP5, 2.7) may be attached without a judgment; another collected non-survivor (seen or stage-1 drop) may be attached as an extra outlet (warning).
Every item source URL equals (after normalisation: tracking parameters, fragment, trailing and repeated slashes) the URL of one of the item's candidates.
No item source URL is an aggregator, cache, archive, AMP, mailing-list or bulletin wrapper (e.g. content.govdelivery.com), shortener, redirect or social URL (FILTER.md 2.7.2, 7.8).
sources[0] is not a paywalled candidate while a non-paywalled candidate is also listed (FILTER.md NP5, 2.9).
A source whose candidate headline was composed by the collector (headline_composed: true, e.g. a CISA KEV entry) carries no headline (FILTER.md 7.8).

Generated text never names or uniquely describes a financial institution (in the claim only while thresholds.json writing.claims_may_name_institutions is false; a warning when true), never states an institution's or the sector's position, and questions, issue statements and rationales never presume the reader's institution type (FILTER.md V3-V5). The other mechanically checkable FILTER.md §7 and §2.9 rules are warnings at publish and errors in selfcheck.mjs.

A URL that is already a source of a published item may be an item source only when the item is a material update (primary judgment dedup material_update) whose match_id is in the same update_of chain as that item; otherwise it is an error (the story is resurfacing: DD_SAME_STORY).
No generated-text field may contain 8 consecutive words of any candidate headline or lead in candidates.json.
All item schema and lint rules of item.schema.json / SPEC §6 apply.

draft_item.description: An Item (item.schema.json) without id, timestamp and backfilled, plus candidate_ids.
